title: paged KV cache: adaptive block allocator reuse + locality-aware pinning optimizations
author: Elena Garcia
release_notes: Adaptive reuse and locality-aware pinning for paged KV cache: reduces eviction churn, improves P95 latency for long-context workloads, and adds observability for allocator decisions.
description: Summary: This PR introduces an adaptive block allocator reuse policy and locality-aware pinning heuristic for the paged KV cache block manager. Motivation: long-context workloads exhibited high eviction/reload churn when working set locality is high but fragmented across blocks. The allocator previously recycled blocks on a simple LRU/age basis which caused unnecessary copy and memory traffic when the same blocks were repeatedly reused across small batched requests. Changes: 1) Adaptive reuse heuristic: the allocator now tracks short-term reuse frequency per block-size bucket and biases reuse towards recently reused blocks when reuse probability for that bucket is high. This reduces allocation churn for common working sets. 2) Locality-aware pinning: when pinning blocks for hot KV entries we now prefer blocks that are co-located in physical GPU memory pools (same memory region/NUMA group) to reduce cross-region data transfers and improve kernel memory locality. 3) TTL demotion: pinning now supports an explicit TTL and demotion path so hot pins decay automatically if not observed as hot. 4) Metrics & tracing: added allocator decision metrics (alloc_attempts, reuse_hits, pin_evictions, locality_hits) and a tracing span around allocation/pinning decisions to help debug regressions. 5) Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for allocator state transitions and integration microbenchmarks that reproduce the earlier thrash case. Backwards compatibility: no KV cache on-disk format changes. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag `kv.adaptive_reuse_v2` and default-enabled for canary nodes. Checklist: - [x] Implement adaptive reuse heuristic - [x] Implement locality-aware pinning and TTL - [x] Add unit/integration tests - [x] Add end-to-end microbench harness and results - [x] Add metrics and tracing - [x] Document config knobs and rollout plan in runtime ops docs Performance: Benchmarks run on a 4xA100 machine with 32k context synthetic load: - Baseline (main prior to this PR): P50=18ms, P95=96ms, throughput=112 req/s - With PR enabled: P50=16ms (-11%), P95=84ms (-12.5%), throughput=122 req/s (+8.9%) Observed reduction in KV eviction events of ~42% in the hotspot test and reduced GPU memcpy bytes by ~30% in the locality-heavy scenario. Memory/regressions: Minor increase in allocator metadata memory (+1.6%) to track reuse stats. No functional changes to API. Implementation notes: - The allocator maintains per-size-bucket circular LRU lists plus a small MRU cache used for reuse biasing. - Locality detection uses existing hw-topology hints from the node agent; when unavailable falls back to previous behavior. - TTL demotion uses an atomic epoch counter sampled on access to avoid expensive timers. Related PRs: PRs touching the paged KV cache are listed in the description (see links in commit messages). See linked Linear ENG-4821 for context and ENG-4987 for rollout tracking. Migration strategy: disabled by default on older release branches; will be enabled behind feature flag for canary then ramp. Implementation is covered by unit and integration tests; see "files_changed" for tests added.
